source.title: Quantifying the Generation Modality Gap in Speech-Text Language Models
source.authors: Ju-Chieh Chou; Jia-Wei Zhou; Karen Livescu

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. One sentence in the FSD discussion is corrupted, and some figure/table content is flattened, but the scaling results in Appendix B are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports speech-model scaling comparisons, but does not test a power-law fit, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or another listed version of the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own genPPL comparisons as model and training-data scale change. These are recorded below as related scaling results, but genPPL is an evaluation metric rather than held-out pretraining loss, and the paper does not fit or evaluate a power law. Other semantic, phonetic, speaker, quality, and emotion results do not measure the claimed scaling laws.
record.test_reason: The study is about the speech-text modality gap. Its only scaling results (Appendix B, Table II) are two-point comparisons of genPPL, a reference-LM perplexity of ASR transcripts of generated continuations. That is not held-out pretraining loss. No power law is fitted or extrapolated, and no allocation or shape analysis is done. With one step per axis, these results cannot show whether downstream performance scales predictably (V6) or whether a power-law form holds in speech (V5).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that an internal text stream substantially reduces the semantic (genPPL) gap, and that phone statistics change only modestly. They find speaker similarity and predicted MOS favour speech-only models, while emotion metrics favour speech-text. They also find the speech-text model closes much of the gap to larger speech-only Llama-Mimi models. They do not call the scaling comparisons 'preliminary'. They say their study uses one model size and one data scale, and list combining their analysis with scaling analyses across modalities as future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares speech-only and speech-text generation systems; it does not apply the original language-model scaling-law fitting method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported genPPL changes differ between speech-only and speech-text models and between data scaling and model scaling.

fits_no_version.finding: Emilia10k to 45k (with 40k to 100k iterations) lowers speech-only genPPL from 182.1 to 149.3, but speech-text genPPL only from 52.7 to 51.6.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In speech LMs, gains in generation coherence from more data shrink when a text stream is added (saturation).

fits_no_version.finding: Going from 456M to 1.16B parameters lowers speech-only genPPL from 182.1 to 170.2, while speech-text genPPL rises from 52.7 to 54.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model-size scaling of transcript-based coherence is weak or non-monotonic for speech-text LMs at this scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Llama-Mimi results evaluated by the authors on Emilia: published 973M gives genPPL 86.5 and published 7.54B gives 52.6. A matched 241M reproduction gives 282.6.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger speech-only codec LMs trained on 240k hours achieve lower genPPL. This rests on non-matched external models.

record.code_released: The paper says the models, code, and evaluation setup will be made publicly available upon publication; no release URL is stated.
record.problems: The scaling comparisons are limited and are not power-law fits; no uncertainty is stated for the Appendix B scaling-table values. The paper itself notes that scaling analyses across modalities remain future work.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version rows were omitted. Other reported metrics and comparisons were left out because they do not measure a listed scaling-law version.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute. Only genPPL is reported, and no fit is made.
Effect of depth, width or other shape choices at fixed parameter count.
Whether a power-law form holds for speech LMs. Two points per axis, no fit.
Predictable downstream improvement with scale. Only single-step comparisons, and no relation to pretraining loss is reported.
Dependence of exponents or allocation on setup or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The study cites Kaplan et al. only for its parameter-counting convention (excluding embedding layers). The Appendix B scaling rows are correctly linked to no version. The data-scaling condition confounds more data with more iterations (40k to 100k). The Llama-Mimi published models were not trained under matched conditions.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of substantially larger-run loss from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Whether a power-law form holds in speech or other modalities and training regimes.
Downstream-task performance scaling or its relationship to pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup or fitting choices.

rows.subject: Base + data scale (speech-only)
rows.operation_detail: Increase training data from Emilia10k to Emilia45k.
rows.note: The paper describes this as a data-scaling result; genPPL is not held-out pretraining loss.
rows.check: Condition is incomplete. Data scaling from Emilia10k to 45k also raised training iterations from 40k to 100k, so data and steps are confounded. A single two-point comparison on genPPL cannot show a power law.

rows.subject: Base + data scale (speech-text)
rows.operation_detail: Increase training data from Emilia10k to Emilia45k.
rows.note: The paper describes the speech-text result as more saturated.
rows.check: Same data-and-iterations confound as r1 (40k to 100k iterations). The change from 52.7 to 51.6 is small, and the authors call the speech-text model more saturated.

rows.subject: Base + model scale (speech-only)
rows.operation_detail: Increase model size from 456M to 1.16B parameters.
rows.note: The paper reports model scaling but does not fit a power law to these results.
rows.check: Backbone moved from OpenELM-270M to 1.1B (456M to 1.16B parameters) at fixed data. This is two points only, with no fit.

rows.subject: Base + model scale (speech-text)
rows.operation_detail: Increase model size from 456M to 1.16B parameters.
rows.note: The paper reports that the speech-text model is more saturated; this comparison does not establish a power-law fit.
rows.check: genPPL worsens slightly (52.7 to 54.5) with the larger model. This is two points only, on a non-loss metric.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
